newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvia still seeking early EU talks.
newsitem.headline: Latvia still seeking early EU talks.

text.p: The Baltic state of Latvia, excluded from a first round of European Union entry talks, said on Wednesday it would aim to meet the criteria before a December meeting of EU nations where a final decision will be taken.

Latvia, a small former Soviet republic on the eastern rim of the Baltic Sea, is one of five eastern European applicant countries which the European Commission declared unready to begin talks on EU membership.
Latvia's neighbour Estonia and four other eastern European countries, Poland, Hungary, the Czech Republic and Slovenia, were judged ready to begin talks.

"We have to mobilise ourselves to prove the readiness of our state to start membership negotiations with the EU before the end of the year," Maris Riekstinsh, foreign ministry state secretary, told a news conference.
Riekstinsh said Latvia would work to meet the criteria and argue its case to EU governments, who will make a final decision on the first wave of accession talks in Luxembourg in December.
He added that the government was disappointed that the commission's decision was not based on latest economic data.
Estonia has for long been seen as the Baltic state which has made the greatest strides in reforming its economy since all three of the small nations quit the former Soviet Union in 1991.
But all three enjoy a degree of macroeconomic stability and standard of living beyond most other former Soviet republics.

The Commission said that Latvia had made considerable progress in forming a market economy but said it would have difficulty coping with competitive pressures and market forces in the union in the medium term.
